subject: Surge SLO handshake & burst activation action items
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Carla Green <carla.green@brightmart.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Surge SLO handshake & burst activation action items

Hi Carla — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can map your SLO requirements to a concrete burst activation plan.

Recap of what we heard (please correct/add):
- p95 latency target for synchronous (non-streaming) calls: ~300ms (goal), 350ms acceptable during sustained traffic.
- Streaming first-token target: <=200ms for interactive flows; follow-on token throughput is less strict but should provide steady delivery for long responses.
- Typical steady-state: ~40 QPS; anticipated short bursts to ~250 concurrent requests lasting 20–45 seconds tied to marketing pushes.
- Median sequence length: ~80 tokens; 95th percentile: ~380 tokens.
- Tolerance for queueing: up to ~10s during extreme bursts, but you prefer graceful degradation & clear throttling thresholds.

Key variables we need from BrightMart before we finalize the test plan:
1) A few representative traffic traces (CSV or pcap) showing RPS over a 2-week window and the largest bursts.
2) Clarify whether streaming traffic constitutes the majority of burst load (estimate % streaming during peak).
3) Any network egress constraints (regions/IP allowlist) and preferred cloud region for testing.

Our immediate proposal (high level):
- Warm pool: maintain 12 prewarmed instances (configurable) to cover expected cold-starts and short spikes with target activation <6s for additional capacity.
- Fast ramp: automated scale-up path to add additional instances within 15–25s for sustained bursts; fallback to queued requests beyond that window.
- Primary SLO gating: p95-latency checks at the model route level; if p95 > target for 3 consecutive minutes we trigger an immediate reroute to a compatible quantized variant and initiate capacity reserve.
- Priming: automated KV-cache priming for the top 50 prompt prefixes (we'll need sample prompts).

Attachments: redwood_burst_test_plan.xlsx (test matrix), example runbook stub.

Next steps / asks (proposed timeline):
- Please send representative traces and confirm region by EOD Wed (Jun 23).
- We propose a scale validation test on Mon Jun 28 (load generator will need IPs).
- Once we have traces, Vivek will map expected warm-pool sizing and Marcus will propose priming sequences.

Thanks — I copied Vivek and Marcus to loop in the implementation owners. If this aligns, I’ll update the test plan and send a calendar invite for the June 28 validation window.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Carla Green <carla.green@brightmart.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@brightmart.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surge SLO handshake & burst activation action items

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirm p95 target: 300ms for non-streaming is ideal; 350ms is our hard limit during short bursts.
- Streaming: first-byte under 200ms is critical for the customer UX. During promotions ~70% of traffic is streaming.
- Concurrency: spikes to 250 concur for 20–30s are realistic (we saw this during last quarter’s campaign).
- Queueing: we can tolerate 8–12s for best-effort requests, but critical calls must be prioritized.

I attached our SLA that shows the campaign windows and some historical spike charts (brightmart_sla.pdf). We can provide sample traffic traces today; I’ll coordinate with ops.

Can you propose what metrics you’ll collect during the validation (latency percentiles, cold-start counts, primed-KV hit rate)? Also, what will the guardrails look like if the platform can’t meet first-byte streaming targets?

Carla Green
Head of Platform Operations, BrightMart
carla.green@brightmart.com

[Attachment: brightmart_sla.pdf (pdf)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Carla Green <carla.green@brightmart.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surge SLO handshake & burst activation action items

Carla — this is perfect, thanks. Quick answers and updated plan based on your clarifications: 

What we will measure during the validation:
- Latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) at model-route level, broken out by streaming vs non-streaming.
- First-token latency distribution for streaming sessions.
- Cold-start count and per-instance activation time.
- KV-cache priming success rate and hit/miss stats for top prefixes.
- Queueing latency and dropped requests.

Guardrails & fallbacks if first-token streaming target is missed: 
1) Immediate short-circuit: route to a smaller, lower-latency model variant for interactive sessions (preserves UX at lower quality).
2) Prioritization: Honor a critical-call header to bypass queueing for priority traffic.
3) Gradual degradation: apply soft-queue limits and return a progressive response indicating degraded mode when queueing exceeds 8s.

Updated actions and owners: 
- BrightMart: send traces + IPs for load generator (Carla) — due Wed Jun 23.
- Redwood (Vivek): map warm-pool sizing and expected activation times using the supplied traces — deliver Jun 25.
- Redwood (Marcus): create priming list and test prompts for KV cache — deliver Jun 25.
- Redwood (Hannah): finalize test plan and calendar invite for Jun 28 validation window — deliver Jun 22.

I attached the updated test matrix (redwood_burst_test_plan.xlsx) and a short runbook. Please confirm the Jun 28 window and we’ll lock it.

Thanks —
Hannah

[Attachment: redwood_burst_test_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surge SLO handshake & burst activation action items

Quick internal note — read and ack:
- Feasible to hit the first-token streaming <200ms for the 12-instance warm pool in us-west-2 assuming priming of top prefixes and persistent model shards.
- Activation behavior: cold-to-ready for extra instances ~12–18s if instance image is warm; additional ~6s for KV priming if network fetches required. We can reduce overall effective activation by prefetching KV and keeping a small reserve of hot shards.
- Fallback plan: automatic reroute to quantized variant will cut p95 by ~120–180ms but may reduce output quality; worth gating to keep user-facing latency safe.

I uploaded a short note on kernel selection and expected perf delta (kernel-selection-notes.txt). Marcus — I’ll sync with you on the exact priming prefixes tonight.

—Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
